text.p: These are the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The United Nations may obliterate any reference to the thorny issue of sovereignty in the second round of talks between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders in order to conclude on an agreement in Montreux.
- The European Commission makes a firm committment that Cyprus will be included in the next enlargement of the European Union.
- European Union's invite to Cyprus angers Turkey, which threatens to unite with the occupied north if the EU opens talks with Cyprus.

- Money laundering report revealed. Confidential report by the intelligence service details attempts by foreigners to sell 600 tonnes of gold through Cyprus last year. The deal fell through when the local bank they tried to do the transaction with declined to take their business.
- Credit card spending rose 27.8 percent in the first half of the year.

- U.S. Presidential emissary on Cyprus Richard Holbrooke is expected to exert pressure on European Union countries to pacify Turkey and its response to the Commission's suggestion that Cyprus be included in the next enlargement.
- Developments on the Cyprus problem are being shifted to Europe. Washington considers Cyprus's accession to the European Union a part of the solution.
- Europe "vetoes" Turkey's accession to the E.U., while Cyprus will be included in the next expansion.
- Athens rules out any acceptance of a clause of the U.N. document on Cyprus which states sovereignty emanates equally from the Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides.
- Five police officers whose promotions were annulled by court amid claims of brutality have been re-promoted by the chief of police.
